metadata.file_name: Noncognitive predictors of mathematics achievement  a machine learning approach using large-scale educational data.pdf
metadata.title: Noncognitive predictors of mathematics achievement: a machine learning approach using large-scale ed
metadata.venue: Journal of Research on Technology in Education

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 background questionnaire derived variables (130 DVs) merged with PISA 2022 cognitive item assignment information to create an individual-level outcome (MS2_LEV) based on whether students received high- vs low-difficulty Stage 2 booklets in the mathematics MSAT. The analytic sample is restricted to students with non-missing values on MATHEFF, HOMEPOS, and ESCS and further excludes medium performers (MS2_LEVMedium), then applies class balancing via NearMiss under-sampling to equalize the low/high classes. The manuscript does not report applying PISA complex survey weights (e.g., student/sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures; therefore, the models appear to be trained on an unweighted, rebalanced dataset. Because decision trees and random forests are used without explicit survey-weight integration, the results should be interpreted as predictive associations within the constructed analytic subset rather than population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not used because the dependent variable is not a PV-based mathematics achievement score; instead, the study defines mathematics achievement at the individual level using MSAT Stage 2 difficulty assignment (MS2_LEV) from the cognitive item data files. Missing data handling is implemented via case exclusion (listwise deletion) for variables used in the ML models (e.g., MATHEFF, HOMEPOS, ESCS), which is explicitly described as removing cases with incomplete responses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Secondary analysis of PISA 2022. The outcome MS2_LEV is defined from the cognitive item data files as the Stage 2 booklet difficulty assignment in the mathematics MSAT: students assigned high-difficulty booklets represent high mathematics performance and those assigned low-difficulty booklets represent low performance; students assigned medium difficulty (MS2_LEVMedium) are excluded. The questionnaire and cognitive files are merged using CNTSTUID. For the information-gain step, 23 variables with no data are removed from the 130 candidate derived variables, and information gain is computed for the remaining 107 variables. For the decision tree and random forest models, cases with missing data on MATHEFF, HOMEPOS, and ESCS are excluded (listwise deletion). Class imbalance is addressed by NearMiss under-sampling to equalize MS2_LEVLow and MS2_LEVHigh, and the final decision-tree/random-forest training/testing uses 80%/20% splits with 10-fold cross-validation. The decision tree uses N=216458 from 71 countries; the random forest uses N=149886 from 71 countries after NearMiss balancing.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (MSAT Stage 2 difficulty assignment; individual-level MS2_LEV)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Decision Tree (CART) — Accuracy: 0.71; Recall: 0.71; Precision: 0.71; F1-Score: 0.71; MCC: 0.42; ROC-AUC: 0.78. (10-fold CV mean F1: 0.7133±0.0040; MCC: 0.4274±0.0081; Accuracy: 0.7134±0.0040.)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics the study leveraged Mathematics self-efficacy, Home possessions, and Socioeconomic status (ESCS) to predict mathematics achievement class (MS2_LEVLow vs MS2_LEVHigh), finding that the decision tree achieved about 71% accuracy and ROC-AUC of 0.78 with Mathematics self-efficacy as the root-level split. This indicates that strengthening students’ mathematics self-efficacy—alongside addressing home resource and socioeconomic disadvantages—may improve the likelihood of achieving higher mathematics performance, though the results are based on a constructed high/low achievement proxy and do not establish causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: The study uses PISA 2022 mathematics data, combining background questionnaire derived variables (130 noncognitive DVs across Student, Financial Literacy, ICT, Well-being, and Parent questionnaires) with cognitive item data to construct an individual-level achievement proxy (MS2_LEV) based on whether students were assigned high- vs low-difficulty Stage 2 booklets in the mathematics MSAT. After excluding medium performers (MS2_LEVMedium) and removing cases with missing values on key predictors (MATHEFF, HOMEPOS, ESCS), the authors balance class imbalance using NearMiss under-sampling and evaluate models with an 80/20 train-test split plus 10-fold cross-validation. The decision tree (CART) using MATHEFF, HOMEPOS, and ESCS achieves ~0.71 accuracy and F1, MCC=0.42, and ROC-AUC=0.78, while information gain and random forest importance rankings consistently place MATHEFF first. Limitations include the use of a constructed high/low achievement label rather than PV-based scores and the lack of reported complex survey-weight application, so findings should be interpreted as predictive associations within the analytic subset.
